title: cost-opt: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Running inference at scale requires conservative defaults for batching and KV prefix caching, but those defaults are often suboptimal across customer workloads. We previously shipped manual tuning and per-customer overrides; this PR introduces an autotune path to surface workload-aware defaults, persistent quantization profiles, and a small unit-economics CLI to make tradeoffs visible to SREs and account teams. Summary of changes: - Add an autotune service that aggregates recent request telemetry and suggests optimal batching and cache window defaults per model class. - Persist quantization profile recommendations (int8/llm-int8/4-bit variants) tied to model metadata and observed token distributions. - Add a unit-economics toolkit CLI (tools/uecon/cli.py) and internal API to estimate per-token cost impact of different profiles and batching/caching choices. - Integrate autotune recommendations into the runtime defaults resolution path with safe fallbacks and rollout flags. - Add e2e integration tests and perf bench harness for evaluating cost vs latency tradeoffs. Backwards compatibility: runtime will continue to honor explicit customer-configured overrides. Autotune recommendations are disabled by default; enable via config flag redwood.autotune.enabled=true and rollout gradually via feature-gates. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-8642) - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Perf benchmarks showing cost improvements - [x] Docs & configuration for ops rollout - [x] Feature gated and off by default Testing and results: Ran perf bench over representative chat/seq-class workloads. Observed median unit-cost reduction of ~10% (8-12% across samples), up to 20% for chat-heavy workloads due to improved prefix caching. P95 latency impact is <1% when using recommended batching sizes and cache windows; worst-case latency regressions are mitigated by fallback to conservative defaults. Rollout plan: enable autotune in staging for two weeks, run monitoring dashboards (redwood.console: autotune.recommendation_impact) and UEs alerting. Then can roll to canary on 5% of traffic, monitor unit-econ dashboards for anomalous regressions before wider rollout. Related work: builds on previous cost-optimization and autotune PRs (see linked Linear ENG-xxxx and previous PR series).

performance_summary: Representative runs across chat and seq workloads show average unit-cost reduction of ~10% (8-12% interquartile). Chat workloads benefit most from longer kv-cache windows and batching; quant profile suggestions reduce GPU memory pressure enabling cheaper instance types in some cases. P95 latency change <1% in Canary runs when autotune recommendations were applied. Recommendation churn is low (<2% weekly) after initial warm-up.
